title: trio-sdk-session-bridge-deprecate-callback-streams-add-typed-asynciterables
author: Maya Kaur
release_notes: Deprecates legacy callback-based streaming APIs in favor of typed async-iterable/pullstream surfaces across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Provides migration guide and examples. Bumps SDK versions: py->1.8.0, ts->2.4.1, go->1.5.0.
description: Context and motivation: We have three parallel streaming surfaces in the SDKs (callback sinks, pull/push helpers, and language-native async iterables). This PR harmonizes ergonomics by deprecating the older callback sink surface and introducing a consistent, typed async-iterable/pullstream contract across Python, TypeScript and Go. The goal is parity for consumer ergonomics and clearer migration path for existing integrations. Design summary: Add typed async iterator wrappers and small adapter layers in each SDK; keep a thin compatibility shim for one release that logs deprecation warnings. Update docs and add migration examples. Checklist: 1) implement async-iterable contracts in py/ts/go; 2) add compatibility shim and deprecation warnings; 3) end-to-end integration tests; 4) update docs/upgrade guide and examples; 5) bump SDK versions; 6) run benchmarks to ensure latency/regressions. Commits summary: feat(py): add AsyncIteratorSession and adapter shim; feat(ts): introduce AsyncGenerator facade and typed stream handles; feat(go): implement PullStreamIterator and Bridge adapter; test: add integration tests that validate resume/cancel semantics; docs: migration guide and examples; ci: bump SDK release matrix for CI. Changed areas: sdk/python/redwood/session_async.py; sdk/python/tests/test_stream_resume.py; sdk/typescript/src/stream/async_generator.ts; sdk/typescript/src/stream/compat_callbacks.ts; sdk/go/stream/iterator.go; sdk/go/stream/bridge.go; docs/upgrades/2024-11-async-iterables.md; examples/streaming/migration/*; changelogs/py-1.8.0.md, ts-2.4.1.md, go-1.5.0.md. Review conversation and resolution: Alex: "Nice cleanup, but we need to ensure the Python iterator preserves cancel semantics and doesn't leak KV cache across resumes." Maya: "Added explicit cancel propagation and integration test test_stream_resume covers cache eviction between resumes." Priya: "TS types look good, but can we keep a tiny compatibility helper for setImmediate-style consumers?" Maya: "Added compat_callbacks.ts which re-exposes the old callback API with deprecation warnings and a runtime opt-in flag. We will remove in the next major release." Liam: "CI failed on Windows for go build initially because of a missing build tag." Maya: "Fixed by adding proper build constraints; re-ran CI." CI summary: initial run had a flaky Go build and one lint warning in TS; all checks pass after fixes. Tests: unit 312 passed, integration 24 passed. Metrics and perf: microbenchmarks show median per-request latency unchanged within noise (±1.5ms) and tail p99 unchanged. Migration guide: docs/upgrades/2024-11-async-iterables.md contains examples in Py/TS/Go and a quick code snippet for converting callback consumers to async iterators. Rollout and compatibility: compatibility shim kept for one minor release; deprecation warnings emitted at runtime in all SDKs. Release impact: bump Python SDK to 1.8.0, TypeScript SDK to 2.4.1, Go SDK to 1.5.0. Merge notes: merged via squash after approvals. Follow-ups: ENG-2042 track removal of compat shim in next major and update partner integrations. Additional notes: flagged release manager to coordinate changelog and approve SDK registry publishing.
